name: New Job Page UI Plan
description: Make the admin job detail page more compact and easier to debug by ordering visible information as a pipeline, while preserving all existing debug data, leaving the token timeline unchanged, and avoiding API server changes.

userStories.title: Build the compact job header and error placement
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the job header to show identity, status, blockers, and primary lifecycle controls in one compact area so I can see start/runtime blockers before reading detailed diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: Widen the job detail page container from `max-w-4xl` to `max-w-7xl` while preserving mobile-safe wrapping and avoiding page-level horizontal overflow.
Rebuild the header to include the project link, full job ID, job status, storage state, project ID, created and updated timestamps, and primary lifecycle actions.
Render action errors, action notices, resume-blocked guidance, `RuntimeModelNotice`, and judging-runtime warnings near the header before detailed debug sections.
Move job errors directly below the header/blocker area and above Work Definition when errors are present.
Add wrapping or break classes for long job IDs, project IDs, action messages, runtime notices, judging-runtime warnings, and job errors.
Do not change API routes, server job/runtime behavior, database schema, or API response contracts.
Do not change the token timeline component, data, content, props, or current page placement.

userStories.title: Create Work Definition and Pipeline Summary sections
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the job's intended work and prompt/request progress summarized before capacity diagnostics so I can understand what the job is processing and where it is in the pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a Work Definition section with provider connection, current request-level LLM call limit, unassessed article count, and token totals.
Keep token totals in Work Definition as their only large metric placement.
Create a Pipeline Summary section with Ready, Claimed, Running, Judged, Skipped, Live Request LLM Calls, Attempts, Failed Attempts, and Anthropic Refusals.
Split the current Job Queue and Request Activity presentations without removing the underlying API data.
Remove duplicate Live Request LLM Calls from the old Job Queue placement because it remains in Pipeline Summary and Provider Capacity Telemetry lifecycle counters.
Use dense metric grids or label/value rows instead of large standalone cards where practical.
Do not change API routes, server job/runtime behavior, database schema, or API response contracts.
Do not change the token timeline component, data, content, props, or current page placement.

userStories.title: Create Request And Capacity Debug section

acceptanceCriteria: Create a Request And Capacity Debug section with Worker Prompt Slots, Worker Queued Prompts, Prompt Prefetch Fill, and Request Slot Waiters.
Make Request Slot Waiters canonical in Request And Capacity Debug and remove the Provider Capacity Telemetry placement if it would otherwise duplicate.
Remove duplicate Worker Prompt Slots and Worker Queued Prompts from the old Job Queue placement because they remain in Request And Capacity Debug and Provider Capacity Telemetry lifecycle counters.
Do not repeat local prompt backlog, request-work backlog, or lifecycle counters in Request And Capacity Debug.
Keep local prompt backlog, request-work backlog, and lifecycle counters canonical in Provider Capacity Telemetry.
Use compact card spacing and wrapping so long metric text does not overflow at mobile widths.

userStories.title: Densify Provider Capacity Telemetry
userStories.description: As an operator, I want provider capacity telemetry to stay complete but denser so I can inspect admission, local worker, aggregate, allocation, bottleneck, and endpoint diagnostics without excessive scrolling.
acceptanceCriteria: Keep Provider Capacity Telemetry visible and preserve endpoint diagnostics, provider coverage, lease/observed mismatch warning, allocation versions, convergence preconditions, bottleneck/subreason/source metadata, and lifecycle counters.

Order Provider Capacity Telemetry sections as Admission Lease Snapshot, Local Worker Diagnostics, Observed Aggregate Telemetry, Allocation State And Convergence, Bottleneck Source Metadata, and Endpoint Diagnostics.
Keep Local Worker Diagnostics as the canonical location for local prompt backlog and request-work backlog.
Keep lifecycle counters only in Provider Capacity Telemetry.
Use denser card padding, grids, and label/value rows without removing fields.
Update telemetry e2e assertions to match final section headings, especially `Admission Lease Snapshot` instead of the older `Lease Authority` label.
Do not change API routes, server job/runtime behavior, database schema, or API response contracts.
Do not change the token timeline component, data, content, props, or current page placement.

userStories.title: Reorder storage diagnostics and actions
userStories.description: As an operator, I want storage, import, lease, repair, and danger controls organized by recovery path so I can diagnose local state before choosing a repair or delete action.
acceptanceCriteria: Reorder Storage And Import Flow by recovery path: storage policy, SQLite/WAL size, outbox/claimed/retained/pending ACK, orphaned local queue, recent transfer flow, oldest unexported/ACK age, projected drain, import success/failure details, and quarantine reason.
Group lease host, PID, lease ID, server job, port, and heartbeat under a compact Runtime Lease subsection.
Remove the duplicate Storage State metric card because storage state remains in the header and storage section badge.
Keep recovery repair actions adjacent to storage diagnostics and do not insert unrelated sections between storage diagnostics and repair controls.
Move delete into a final separated Danger Actions section below recovery actions.
Add wrapping or break classes for lease IDs, endpoint URLs, provider keys, import failure details, quarantine reasons, and storage/recovery messages.
